items.review_rationale: Read anchored Lipschitz property with one fixed point a, one global constant L, and comparison against every x, deliberately not equating to pairwise global Lipschitzness.

references.context: One fixed a∈X; choose L≥0 such that d_Y(f(x),f(a))≤L d_X(x,a) for every x∈X.

references.phrase: anchored not local or global pairwise condition
references.disposition: Anchored condition compares only against fixed a and need not imply same bound for arbitrary x,y.

items.review_rationale: Read globally Lipschitz mapping between metric spaces using a single nonnegative constant for all pairs of input points, distinguishing the anchored variant.

references.context: A single nonnegative real L such that for all x,y, d_Y(f(x),f(y))≤L d_X(x,y).

references.phrase: global condition has two freely varying points
references.disposition: One L for all pairs; stronger than restriction to one fixed reference point.

items.review_rationale: Read graph-theoretic unrooted tree as connected simple undirected graph with no nontrivial closed edge-trail (circuit), retaining distinction from directed/rooted trees.

references.context: Closed walk using each traversed edge at most once, with positive length, in a simple undirected graph.

references.disposition: Acyclic graph property; a rooted orientation is not part of the definition.

items.review_rationale: Read equivalent tree criterion using simple connected graph with no cycles, keeping cycle meaning distinct from arbitrary closed walk with repeated edges.

references.context: Nontrivial closed graph path without repeated internal vertices, in simple undirected context.

references.disposition: No cycle with simple connectivity, not an orientation or root condition.
